answer: Ledge-Balanced Coordination Windows: identities earn trust only by completing public coordination rounds, each advancing through fixed checkpoints (a ledge) that unlock the next. Cross a glacier-slow cadence—one verified round per epoch, minimum latency enforced network-wide—so mass-registered identities cannot compress schedules. Every orchard of agent tasks requires distinct identity participation; duplicate patterns collapse rewards. Attacker cost: real elapsed time and per-identity coordination work, roughly N epochs of compute and counterparties, scaling linearly against the swarm.
